question: An 18-year-old boy who went to the emergency room due to pain and functional impotence in the right knee. After the biopsy study, the diagnosis of osteoblastic osteosarcoma of the distal femur is established. Given the type of tumor and the location, what treatment protocol is usually performed in most cases?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Osteoblastic osteosarcoma diagnosis" -> "Common treatment protocol" -> "Neoadjuvant chemotherapy" -> "Surgery" -> "Adjuvant chemotherapy" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Osteoblastic osteosarcoma diagnosis" -> "Consider limb-sparing options" -> "Neoadjuvant chemotherapy" -> "Surgery" -> "Adjuvant chemotherapy" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Osteoblastic osteosarcoma diagnosis" -> "Assess need for limb preservation" -> "Amputation" -> "Possible" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Osteoblastic osteosarcoma diagnosis" -> "Consider radiation therapy" -> "Radiation therapy and chemotherapy" -> "Unclear" -> 40%
analysis: Osteosarcoma, particularly in the distal femur, is typically treated with a combination of chemotherapy and surgery. The standard treatment protocol involves neoadjuvant chemotherapy to shrink the tumor, followed by surgical resection, and then adjuvant chemotherapy to eliminate any remaining cancer cells. This approach aims to preserve the limb and improve survival rates. Amputation is less common now due to advances in limb-sparing surgeries. Radiation therapy is not typically used as osteosarcoma is not very sensitive to it.
